claims.claim: The page is a complete history of the FISA Title VII sunset clause since 2008
claims.sourceSpan: effective December 31, 2012, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, as amended by section 101(a), is repealed

claims.claim: Section 702 sits inside Title VII of FISA
claims.sourceSpan: SUBCHAPTER VI - ADDITIONAL PROCEDURES REGARDING CERTAIN PERSONS OUTSIDE THE UNITED STATES

claims.claim: Title VII was created with a repeal clause attached, section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008
claims.sourceSpan: Pub. L. 110–261, title IV, §403(b)(1), July 10, 2008, 122 Stat. 2474

claims.claim: Section 702 is codified at 50 U.S.C. 1881a
claims.sourceSpan: Sec. 1881a - Procedures for targeting certain persons outside the United States other than United States persons

claims.claim: The Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence jointly authorize, for up to one year at a time, the targeting of people reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly, for a period of up to 1 year from the effective date of the authorization, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information

claims.claim: The statute states that nothing in FISA subchapter I requires an application for a court order for such an acquisition
claims.sourceSpan: Nothing in subchapter I shall be construed to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States.

claims.claim: The two officials may direct an electronic communication service provider in writing to immediately provide the Government with all information, facilities, or assistance necessary
claims.sourceSpan: may direct, in writing, an electronic communication service provider to— (A) immediately provide the Government with all information, facilities, or assistance necessary to accomplish the acquisition

claims.claim: An acquisition may not intentionally target any person known at the time to be located in the United States
claims.sourceSpan: may not intentionally target any person known at the time of acquisition to be located in the United States

claims.claim: An acquisition may not target a person abroad when the purpose is to target a particular known person in the United States
claims.sourceSpan: if the purpose of such acquisition is to target a particular, known person reasonably believed to be in the United States

claims.claim: An acquisition may not intentionally target a United States person reasonably believed to be outside the United States
claims.sourceSpan: may not intentionally target a United States person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

claims.claim: An acquisition may not intentionally acquire a communication whose sender and all intended recipients are known to be in the United States
claims.sourceSpan: may not intentionally acquire any communication as to which the sender and all intended recipients are known at the time of the acquisition to be located in the United States

claims.claim: An acquisition may not intentionally acquire communications that contain a reference to, but are not to or from, a target
claims.sourceSpan: may not intentionally acquire communications that contain a reference to, but are not to or from, a target of an acquisition authorized under subsection (a)

claims.claim: An acquisition must be conducted in a manner consistent with the Fourth Amendment
claims.sourceSpan: shall be conducted in a manner consistent with the fourth amendment to the Constitution of the United States

claims.claim: The Attorney General must adopt querying procedures for information collected under Section 702
claims.sourceSpan: shall adopt querying procedures consistent with the requirements of the fourth amendment to the Constitution of the United States for information collected pursuant to an authorization under subsection (a)

claims.claim: Those procedures must keep a record of each United States person query term used
claims.sourceSpan: include a technical procedure whereby a record is kept of each United States person query term used for a query

claims.claim: FBI personnel must obtain prior supervisor or attorney approval for a United States person query of unminimized Section 702 material
claims.sourceSpan: Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel must obtain prior approval from a Federal Bureau of Investigation supervisor (or employee of equivalent or greater rank) or attorney who is authorized to access unminimized contents or noncontents obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a) for any query of such unminimized contents or noncontents made using a United States person query term.

claims.claim: That approval requirement has a threat-to-life exception
claims.sourceSpan: reasonable belief that conducting the query could assist in mitigating or eliminating a threat to life or serious bodily harm

claims.claim: FBI queries solely designed to find and extract evidence of criminal activity are prohibited
claims.sourceSpan: shall prohibit queries of information acquired under subsection (a) that are solely designed to find and extract evidence of criminal activity

claims.claim: There is a litigation and discovery exception to that prohibition
claims.sourceSpan: such query is necessary to identify information that must be produced or preserved in connection with a litigation matter or to fulfill discovery obligations

claims.claim: REMOVED FROM PROSE: the FBI is the only agency the query subsection names - contradicted by 1881a(f)(3)(D)(vi), which names the Office of Personnel Management inside that same subsection.
claims.sourceSpan: such as those classified by the Office of Personnel Management as Presidential Appointment with Senate Confirmation

claims.claim: The FISA Amendments Act of 2008 became Public Law 110-261 on July 10, 2008
claims.sourceSpan: Pub. L. 110–261, title IV, §403(b)(1), July 10, 2008, 122 Stat. 2474

claims.claim: Section 403(b)(1) provided that except as provided in section 404, effective December 31, 2012, Title VII of FISA is repealed
claims.sourceSpan: Except as provided in section 404, effective December 31, 2012, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, as amended by section 101(a), is repealed.

claims.claim: A second paragraph applied the same date to technical and conforming amendments
claims.sourceSpan: Technical and conforming amendments</header><text>Effective December 31, 2012

claims.claim: One of those conforming amendments touches the federal criminal wiretap statute
claims.sourceSpan: paragraph (2)(a)(ii)(A) of this section is amended by striking "or a court order pursuant to section 704 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978"

claims.claim: The reverse-targeting limit was in the 2008 Act from the start
claims.sourceSpan: may not intentionally target a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States if the purpose of such acquisition is to target a particular, known person reasonably believed to be in the United States

claims.claim: Section 404 of the same Act carries transition procedures under which orders, authorizations and directives already issued under Title VII survive a repeal until they expire
claims.sourceSpan: shall continue in effect until the date of the expiration of such order, authorization, or directive.

claims.claim: Section 404 also carried over orders issued under section 105B of FISA as added by the Protect America Act of 2007
claims.sourceSpan: any order, authorization, or directive issued or made pursuant to section 105B of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 [50 U.S.C. 1805b], as added by section 2 of the Protect America Act of 2007

Round 3: ZERO factual defects, 93/93 spans verbatim, plus 4 scope/wording observations - all four applied. Round 4 confirmed the four edits.
